# Fears to Fathom: Woodbury Getaway Co-op Mod

unofficial co-op multiplayer mod for **Fears to Fathom: Woodbury Getaway**. Host runs the real game; a second player joins, and the scripted scares happen to both of you in sync.

## Status

Cabin has the most coverage. Pizzeria, RoadTrip, Office and ParkingLot have working sync foundations. Full story parity is being built scene by scene. See the [live roadmap](https://tudorek12345.github.io/fears-to-fathom-woodbury-getaway-mp-mod/#roadmap) for what's coming next.

## Install and play

Download the [current test package](https://tudorek12345.github.io/fears-to-fathom-woodbury-getaway-mp-mod/downloads/woodbury-coop-latest.7z). Its [build manifest](https://tudorek12345.github.io/fears-to-fathom-woodbury-getaway-mp-mod/downloads/build-info.json) records the version, protocol, checksums, and validation limits.

1. Each player needs their own Windows/Steam game installation.
2. Extract the archive contents into the game root. `winhttp.dll`, `doorstop_config.ini`, and `BepInEx/` must be beside the game executable. The loader is included.
3. Launch and press **F11**. One player selects `CoopHost`; the other selects `CoopClient` and enters the host IP.
4. For internet play, make TCP **27055** and UDP **27056** reachable or use a virtual LAN. Steam friend invites/relay are not implemented.

Use the same package on both machines. Back up a custom mod config before replacing it. The test package disables the forced Cabin test start. **F8** opens diagnostics; **F10** captures scene state; **F12** toggles available passenger seats.

The current build compiles and passes snapshot/log regression checks. It still needs a complete paired story run. Historical July 8 logs confirm a Cabin client catch and mirrored native death; full save/resume, reconnect correctness, and all endings remain validation/development work.

## Build and verify

Requires a .NET SDK, BepInEx 5 Mono, and local game/Unity reference assemblies:

```powershell
.\scripts\CopyLibs.ps1 -GameDir "<GameDir>"
.\scripts\Build.ps1
.\scripts\Test-SyncRegression.ps1
```

The DLL is written to `src/WoodburySpectatorSync/bin/Release/net472/WoodburySpectatorSync.dll`.

For a manual paired gameplay test:

```powershell
.\scripts\Launch-CoopPair.ps1 -GameDir "<GameDir>" -AutoStartHost -AutoConnectClient -EnableSessionLog
.\scripts\Check-CoopLogs.ps1 -GameDir "<GameDir>" -RequireTraffic -RequireGameplay
```

Enter gameplay on the host; remaining at the menu does not pass the gameplay smoke check. Use `-Since <run-start-time>` to restrict checks to the current run. `Compare-SceneDiscoveryDump.ps1` compares F10 host/client dumps.

## Package the test build

```powershell
.\scripts\Build-TestPackage.ps1 -LoaderRoot "<clean BepInEx overlay root>"
.\scripts\Update-SiteData.ps1
```

The loader root must contain `winhttp.dll`, `doorstop_config.ini`, and `BepInEx/core/`. Packaging builds from source, checks the actual DLL version, runs regressions, and writes the archive plus manifest under `site/downloads/`. GitHub Pages deployment rejects an archive whose hash or version disagrees with that manifest/source.

See `CHANGELOG.md` for implementation history.
